claims.text: Conventional TOR-TILD EAM references inadequately represent the diversity of atomic configurations in an ab initio HEA liquid.
This inadequate representation produces a larger thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed intervention is to train an ML interatomic potential on high-temperature, multicomponent ab initio configurations, particularly liquid configurations.
Neural-network and moment-tensor potentials are candidate forms of the proposed ML interatomic potential.
Training on high-temperature liquid configurations will allow the ML potential to represent the ab initio liquid's distribution of atomic configurations better than an EAM reference.
A liquid-enriched training set will enable the ML model to capture complex many-body interactions in a high-entropy alloy.
Better representation of configurations and many-body interactions will improve phase-space overlap between the ML reference and the ab initio target.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The proposed ML reference may reduce TI path mismatch by 20–30% relative to EAM-based methods.
Reduced TI path mismatch will yield more reliable solid- and liquid-phase free-energy calculations.
The proposed method is applicable to near-equiatomic HEAs at or near their melting temperatures.
The proposed comparison applies to both solid and liquid phases near melting.
Efficacy for off-equiatomic compositions or lower temperatures is untested.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction will vary with alloy composition, temperature, and the quality of the ab initio training data.

The hypothesis is falsified if the ML-IAP improves TI path mismatch by less than approximately 10% relative to the TOR-TILD EAM control or fails to move free-energy estimates closer to ab initio benchmarks.
